newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates mixed, active regions firmer.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates mixed, active regions firmer.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rate direction was mixed, but rates for more active cross Med and West African fixings continued to edge higher, brokers said.
Activity was generally thin with few fresh fixings seen in most regions, particularly for tonnage above Suezmax.
Rates for transatlantic voyages from West Africa continued to firm with few modern cargoes seen to the end of the month.

No new VLCC fixings were seen moving transatlantic, but a cargo near Suezmax was booked from Forcados to Uruguay at W95, while the market into UKC was weaker with a cargo booked into Pembroke at W90 around 7-1/2 points under Wednesday's levels.
Inter UK/Cont fixings were slower after a flurry of trade on Wednesday but rates held firm at values around W102.5.
Several Aframax cargoes were fixed into U.K. and continental refiners and a Petrochemical end-user.
A Suezmax cargo was also done at a firm W100 into UKC.
Transatlantic business from the North Sea remained thin with rates for VLCCs pegged around W62.5 and Suezmax around W80.
The Western Hemisphere market saw Caribs upcoast trade at a steady W135 for 70,000 tonnes with fuel oil trading into the U.S. Gulf at W130.

Middle East Gulf activity remained thin. No new fixings for Japan or the recently active South Korean market were reported, but traders valued rates steady with Japan voyages for VLCCs pegged around W62.5 in line with the last trade on Monday at W62.75 and South Korean VLCC deliveries around W59.5.
A VLCC was booked to Singapore but no rate was reported.
Cross Mediterranean activity were also slower. Rates for Aframax cargoes held around W97.50 and Suezmax vessels took a slightly firmer W88.
